thesis: Nuh's obedience under repeated elite mockery is a test of certainty, and the ridicule will be reversed when the punishment lands publicly and permanently on the mockers.
notes: All four editions carry the thesis. al-Tabari: 'فيقول لهم نوح: إن تسخروا منا... فإنا نهزأ منكم في الآخرة، كما تهزءون منا في الدنيا'; al-Muyassar: 'فإنا نسخر منكم غدًا عند الغرق'; al-Jalalayn: 'إذا نجونا وغرقتم'; Ibn Kathir on 11:38 'This is a severe threat and a serious warning' and on yukhzihi 'it will humiliate him in this life', matching the file's public-disgrace-then-lasting-punishment reading. No countable/absolute claims in the file (verified by sweep). al-Jalalayn's 'حكاية حال ماضية' on wa yasna'u supports the file's 'ongoing form / we watch the process' point. Two non-blocking observations for the human reviewer, neither an error: (1) Part 1 section 3 reframes 'we will mock you' as 'the exposure of false mockery' rather than the literal reciprocal mockery the four sources describe (mocking them at the drowning / in the akhirah) — the gloss is compatible but under-reports the plain classical reading; a half-sentence naming the classical sense would tighten it. (2) The file says 'Hud teaches...' and 'Hud leaves us with...' meaning Surah Hud; since a prophet named Hud exists, 'Surah Hud' would remove the ambiguity. Note also the file imports none of al-Tabari's ark israʼiliyyat (dimensions, the elephant/lion reports, Ibn Ishaq's Torah material) — correct restraint, since al-Tabari himself dismisses those as 'رجم من رجم أصحاب الكتب السالفة'.

thesis: Fir'awn's court, unable to answer Musa's signs, relabels him as a skilled magician, recasts revelation as a territorial/security threat, then delays and mobilizes to absorb the confrontation on its own terms.
notes: The one named attribution checks out verbatim. The file says 'As al-Tabari notes, this is the moment the discourse turns to Fir'awn consulting his council: what do you advise, what should be done with this matter?' — al-Tabari on 7:110: 'وقال فرعون للملأ "فماذا تأمرون" يقول: فأي شيء تأمرون أن نفعل في أمره؟ بأي شيء تشيرون فيه؟', and he then discusses the unmarked speaker change (comparing it to 12:51-52). al-Muyassar agrees: 'قال فرعون: فبماذا تشيرون عليَّ أيها الأشراف'. Thesis grounded in Ibn Kathir 7:109-110 ('They held counsel to decide what they should do about Musa... They feared that he might lure people to his side by his magic... and drive them away from their land') and al-Tabari on 7:111 (Ibn Abbas: أخِّره; Qatadah: احبسه) and hashirin = gatherers/الشُّرَط (Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Muyassar), matching the file's 'label, alarm, delay, organize'. No countable/absolute claims. One non-blocking observation: the frontmatter/body translation renders all of 7:109-110 including 'so what do you command?' as the chiefs' speech, while Part 1 section 3 follows al-Tabari in assigning that clause to Fir'awn; the two readings sit side by side without a note, and al-Jalalayn on 7:109 flags the same issue ('وفي الشعراء أنه من قول فرعون نفسه فكأنهم قالوه معه على سبيل التشاور'). One clause acknowledging the speaker ikhtilaf would remove the inconsistency. al-Jalalayn 7:110 FETCH FAILED — unknown, not confirmation; nothing in the file depends on it.

thesis: Yusuf's refusal in the locked room came not from willpower but from running to Allah (ma'adh Allah) and being held by divine intervention (burhan / mukhlasin), while the torn shirt shows physical evidence outlasting the guilty party's narrative.

flags.quote: *Qaddat* — Form II of ق د د — to tear, to rip. Intensive form: this was a forceful grab, not a gentle tug.
flags.issue: FALSE morphology. quranic-corpus.json 12:25:3:2 gives قَدَّتْ as 'PERF|VF:1|ROOT:قدد' — Form I, not Form II (compare 12:23:8:2 غَلَّقَتِ 'PERF|VF:2', where the file's identical intensive-form argument is correct). The passive قُدَّ at 12:26:13:1, 12:27:4:1, 12:28:4:1 is likewise VF:1. The whole inference 'Intensive form: this was a forceful grab, not a gentle tug' rests on the wrong form and does not survive. Fix: either drop the form claim and argue the force from the narrative (Ibn Kathir: 'tearing it so terribly that it fell off Yusuf's back'), or correct it to Form I.

flags.quote: *Hamma biha* — he inclined toward her. The Quran does not deny this. It presents it honestly: he was human, the conditions were extreme, the desire was real.
flags.issue: Adab/ikhtilaf gap on the passage's known crux, stated as settled fact about a prophet's inner state. The file's own translation (frontmatter and body) uses the lawla-fronting rendering — 'he would have desired her had he not seen the proof of his Lord' — which is the reading that avoids saying the hamm actualized, so the file contradicts itself on the exact clause. The fetched sources show a live ikhtilaf that the file never surfaces: Ibn Kathir on 12:24 reports it via al-Baghawi as 'about the thoughts that cross the mind' and adds 'It was also reported that the Ayah means that Yusuf was about to beat her'; al-Tabari affirms the hamm of both ('أخبر عن همِّ يوسف وامرأة العزيز كل واحد منهما بصاحبه'). One sentence naming the ikhtilaf and distinguishing tadabbur from a verdict on 'ismah is required before this ships.

flags.quote: he is alone in a house with the woman who owns him
flags.issue: Extra-textual and contradicted by the sources. The 'Aziz, not his wife, is the buyer and master: al-Jalalayn glosses 'إنه ربي' as 'الذي اشتراني... سيدي' (the one who bought me, my master), al-Tabari 'إن صاحبك وزوجك سيدي' with three asanid (al-Suddi, Ibn Abi Najih, Mujahid), and 12:25 itself calls the 'Aziz 'سَيِّدَهَا' — her master. Repeated at 'She was his owner.' and 'He is her property.' The theme built on it ('a slave-owner dynamic', 'potentially fatal') is a modern socio-legal reconstruction, not a Quranic or classical statement. Fix: recast as 'the wife of the man who owns him' / 'the mistress of the household'.

flags.quote: classical scholars differ on whether it refers to Allah or to the 'Aziz (the master of the house)
flags.issue: Unverified attribution to the classical tradition. All four fetched editions give only the 'Aziz reading: Ibn Kathir ('as they used to call the chief and master a Rabb... This was said by Mujahid, As-Suddi, Muhammad bin Ishaq and several others'), al-Tabari (athar 19002-19004: 'سيدي'), al-Jalalayn ('الذي اشتراني... سيدي'). The 'Allah' reading exists in later tafsir but is not carried by any source fetched here, so 'Both readings are true simultaneously. ... The ambiguity is load-bearing' overstates what can be shown. Fix: attribute the 'Aziz reading to the named salaf and present the Allah reading as a minority/later view, or cite a source that carries it.

flags.quote: He is beautiful — the Quran has told us this
flags.issue: Sequencing error. At 12:23 the Quran has not stated Yusuf's beauty; it conveys it at 12:31, after this scene, through the women of the city. Ibn Kathir supplies it here as tafsir ('Yusuf was very handsome, filled with manhood and beauty'), which is a different warrant from 'the Quran has told us'. Fix: attribute to the tafsir, or forward-reference 12:31.

flags.quote: This is Form III — *fa'ala* — which in Arabic indicates an action directed **toward** another person, a relational verb.
flags.issue: The form identification is right (corpus 12:23:1:2 رَٰوَدَتْ = 'PERF|VF:3'), but the pattern is mislabelled: Form III is fā'ala (مُفاعَلة), while fa'ala is the Form I pattern. In a file whose method is morphological transparency this misleads. Fix: change 'fa'ala' to 'fā'ala'.

flags.quote: the most psychologically detailed narrative in the Quran
flags.issue: Unverifiable superlative in passage_context; not mechanically checkable and not attributed. Fix: soften to 'one of the most detailed' or drop.

notes: Thesis itself is sound and classically carried — do not rewrite the file. Ibn Kathir on 12:24 ('Just as We showed him the evidence that turned him away from that sin, We save him from all types of evil... Mukhlasin: chosen, purified, designated'), and the qira'at claim VERIFIES: al-Tabari 'فقرأته عامة قرأة المدينة والكوفة ... بفتح اللام' vs 'بعض قرأة البصرة ... بكسر اللام', and corpus 12:24:19:2 مُخْلَصِينَ = 'PASS_PCPL|VF:4' — so 'the majority reading is mukhlasin — passive' stands. The count claim 'The shirt appears four times in these seven verses' VERIFIES: قمص at 12:25, 12:26, 12:27, 12:28 (root قمص occurs 6x Quran-wide: 12:18, 25, 26, 27, 28, 12:93). 'Hayta lak / hi'tu laka' VERIFIES against Ibn Kathir (Ibn Abbas, Abu Wa'il, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah read it as 'I am ready for you'). The 'Aziz as speaker of 12:29 and his preference for silence VERIFIES against Ibn Kathir ('The 'Aziz ordered Yusuf to be discrete... do not mention to anyone what has happened. The 'Aziz was an easy man') — worth knowing that al-Tabari instead reports from Ibn Abbas that 12:29 is the witness's speech, so the file follows one of two documented views; acceptable as written. ISRAʼILIYYAT CHECK: CLEAN. The file imports none of it — no Ya'qub biting his finger (al-Tabari 19013 from al-Suddi, and Ibn Ishaq 19014), no undressing detail, no naming of the wife (al-Jalalayn: زُلَيْخا), no infant-in-the-cradle witness. Its burhan is left unspecified ('a light placed in the moment of maximum darkness'), which matches Ibn Jarir's own ruling as Ibn Kathir relays it: 'There are no clear proofs to support any of these statements in specific, so it should be left vague, as Allah left it.' Its 'wise man of her household' framing matches the majority (Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Ibn Ishaq per Ibn Kathir), though the reviewer should know al-Tabari preferred the cradle-infant view. No truncation artifacts; the file quotes no tafsir blocks. Actionable fix list, in order: correct the qaddat Form II error, add one ikhtilaf sentence on the hamm clause of 12:24, then the four minors.
